headline: Govt cancels health workers' leave in 11 flood-hit districts
summary: Health Minister Sardar Mohammad Sakhavat Hossain says maximum preparation has been taken to ensure continuous healthcare services for flood-affected people.
details: The government has canceled the leave of all health workers in 11 flood-hit districts to ensure uninterrupted healthcare services in the field.
Health Minister Sardar Mohammad Sakhavat Hossain announced this during a press conference at the Secretariat on Monday, stating that no patient should be deprived of treatment.
The 11 districts include Chattogram, Cox's Bazar, Bandarban, Rangamati, Khagrachhari, Feni, Noakhali, Lakshmipur, Chandpur, Cumilla, and Brahmanbaria.
Medical teams have been deployed and stocks of essential medicines, saline, water purification tablets, and anti-snake venom have been ensured.
Special attention is being given to pregnant women, children, and people in remote areas. A senior physician has been assigned to monitor the overall health situation in each district.

Health Secretary Mo. Kamruzzaman Chowdhury stated that 95 snakebite victims have already been treated and recovered. Over 1,000 vials of anti-snake venom are currently in stock, with 25,000 more arriving within 15 days.
The DGPH Director General Professor Prabhat Chandra Biswas mentioned that health information and advice are being provided via the national health service call center 16263 and the Health Batayon.
An emergency control room (01759114488) has also been opened by the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) to monitor the situation.
caption:
No patient left behind: The government has canceled leave for all health workers in 11 flood-hit districts to ensure emergency care.

The government has canceled the leave of all health workers in 11 flood-hit districts to ensure uninterrupted healthcare services in the field.

Health Minister Sardar Mohammad Sakhavat Hossain announced this during a press conference at the Secretariat on Monday, stating that no patient should be deprived of treatment.

The 11 districts include Chattogram, Cox's Bazar, Bandarban, Rangamati, Khagrachhari, Feni, Noakhali, Lakshmipur, Chandpur, Cumilla, and Brahmanbaria.

Medical teams have been deployed and stocks of essential medicines, saline, water purification tablets, and anti-snake venom have been ensured.

Special attention is being given to pregnant women, children, and people in remote areas. A senior physician has been assigned to monitor the overall health situation in each district.

Health Secretary Mo. Kamruzzaman Chowdhury stated that 95 snakebite victims have already been treated and recovered. Over 1,000 vials of anti-snake venom are currently in stock, with 25,000 more arriving within 15 days.

The DGPH Director General Professor Prabhat Chandra Biswas mentioned that health information and advice are being provided via the national health service call center 16263 and the Health Batayon.

An emergency control room (01759114488) has also been opened by the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) to monitor the situation.

headline: Trump announces naval blockade of Iran and 20% toll on ships
summary: US President Donald Trump claims the US will act as the 'guardian' of the Strait of Hormuz, charging ships for security services.
details: US President Donald Trump has announced the implementation of a new naval blockade against Iran, claiming the US will take full responsibility for the security of the Strait of Hormuz.

Trump stated in a telephone interview with Fox News and a post on Truth Social that the US will act as the 'guardian' of the {// a bit of the route} the strait, charging a 20% toll on every cargo ship passing through to cover security costs.
The US President accused Iran of violating an interim agreement, stating that Iran 'always breaks' agreements and that the US will now launch 'very harsh attacks' on the country.

Iran has immediately rejected the US announcement. A spokesperson for the Central Command of Iran's Armed Forces, Ibrahim Zolfaqari, warned that any US role in managing the strait strait is unacceptable and any cooperation with US forces would be considered a war against Iranian sovereignty.

Tensions have escalated further as Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) claimed attacks on US military installations in Bahrain and Kuwait, while the US has targeted several military targets in southern Iran, including air defense systems and coastal radars.
An interim agreement signed last month aimed to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and implement a ceasefire, but recent clashes have made the future of that agreement uncertain.
